q: 中级候选人挂掉系统设计面试最常见的原因是？
options: 算 QPS/DAU 时出了算术错误
选用了不够『潮』的数据库
没能交付出一个可运行的完整系统
白板图画得不够美观
options_en: Made an arithmetic mistake estimating QPS or DAU.
Picked a database that felt unfashionable.
Failed to deliver a working, complete system.
The whiteboard diagram wasn't pretty enough.
why: 最容易自毁的方式是没能交付出可工作的系统；这是中级候选人最常见的挂点，表面上常被误诊为『时间管理』问题。
why_en: The single easiest way to fail is not delivering a working system, which mid-level candidates most often misdiagnose as a time-management problem.
optionMeanings: 把失利归因于估算数字算错，一种常见误解
把失利归因于数据库选型不够新潮
指方案从未落成一个能跑通的整体架构
把失利归因于画图美观度
optionScenarioImpacts: 算术小错通常能当场纠正，不是致命伤
选型有争议时考官通常接受多种数据库
半成品设计让考官无法评估你端到端的判断力
美观从不是评分项，考官在意逻辑而非配色
optionDirectness: 不直接：算术失误可修正，不是主因。
不直接：数据库选择很少是单一死因。
最直接：未交付完整系统是中级候选人最常见的挂点。
不直接：外观从不是评分维度。
optionMeanings_en: Blames failure on a miscalculated number, a common misread.
Blames failure on the database choice feeling outdated.
Means the design never became one runnable end-to-end system.
Blames failure on how tidy the diagram looks.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A small arithmetic slip is usually fixable on the spot.
Interviewers generally accept several reasonable databases.
An unfinished design leaves the interviewer nothing end-to-end to judge.
Neatness was never a scored dimension.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: arithmetic slips are correctable, not the main cause.
Not direct: database choice is rarely the single cause.
Most direct: failing to finish is the most common mid-level failure.
Not direct: appearance is never a scoring axis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统每秒处理的查询次数，衡量负载的常用单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS is the number of queries a system handles per second, a standard load metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每天实际使用产品的独立用户数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU is the count of unique users who use the product on a given day.

q: 所谓「时间管理差」的真相通常是什么？
options: 不是要快一倍，而是要把时间花在对的事情上
确实需要说话语速更快
是面试给的时间本身不够
是面试官计时不准确
options_en: It's not about working twice as fast, but focusing on the right things.
You really do need to talk faster.
The interview simply doesn't allocate enough time.
The interviewer's timing is inaccurate.
why: 问题往往不是速度，而是聚焦：把精力放在考官最看重的部分，就不需要『工作快两倍』。
why_en: The issue is rarely that you must work twice as fast; usually you just need to focus on the right things.
optionMeanings: 把『慢』重新定义为『没聚焦重点』
把『慢』归因于语速这个表层现象
把『慢』归因于外部时间预算
把『慢』归因于考官的计时工具
optionScenarioImpacts: 提示你该练的是筛选优先级，不是加速动作
光说得快不会让设计更完整，只会更乱
45 分钟对所有候选人一样长，抱怨没用
计时误差不会系统性地拖垮候选人
optionDirectness: 最直接：聚焦对的事才是根因。
不直接：语速快不解决方向错的问题。
不直接：所有候选人共用同一时长。
不直接：计时工具不是失败的系统性原因。
optionMeanings_en: Reframes slowness as a lack of focus, not a speed problem.
Blames slowness on the surface symptom of talking pace.
Blames slowness on the fixed external time budget.
Blames slowness on the interviewer's timing tool.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Points you toward practicing prioritization, not speed.
Talking faster alone won't make the design more complete.
Everyone gets the same forty-five minutes, so this isn't fixable.
Timing error isn't a systematic cause of failure.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: focusing on the right things is the root cause.
Not direct: faster speech doesn't fix a wrong focus.
Not direct: the time budget is fixed for everyone.
Not direct: timing tools aren't a systematic failure cause.

q: 跟随交付框架（Delivery Framework）的好处有哪些？（多选）
options: 始终聚焦在面试官最看重的部分
紧张、被问懵时有清晰的回退路径
线性搭建方案，不容易迷路、不容易卡死
保证一定拿到 offer
options_en: Keeps you focused on what the interviewer cares about most.
Gives you a clear fallback path when you freeze up under nerves.
Builds the solution linearly, so you rarely get lost or stuck.
Guarantees you'll get the offer.
why: 框架 = 一套推荐的步骤与时间分配：让你聚焦重点、慌乱时有轨道可退、并线性搭建方案——但它不是 offer 保票。
why_en: The framework keeps you focused on what matters, gives you a track to fall back on when nervous, and helps you build the solution linearly.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    F["Framework"] --> P["Focus"]
    F --> R["Fallback path"]
    F --> C["Complete system"]
optionMeanings: 框架把注意力锚定在考官的评分点上
框架提供固定步骤，慌乱时可以照抄流程
框架按顺序搭建，避免同时改十个地方
误把『有方法论』等同于『必过』
optionScenarioImpacts: 省下判断『该讲什么』的决策成本
紧张时仍能按部就班完成设计
每一步都建立在前一步之上，减少推倒重来
过度依赖框架会让人忽视实际设计质量
optionDirectness: 最直接：这是框架的核心价值之一。
最直接：框架本来就是为了应对慌乱设计的。
最直接：线性推进正是框架的结构本身。
不直接：框架只是方法论，不是结果保证。
optionMeanings_en: The framework anchors attention on what interviewers score.
It supplies fixed steps to follow when you panic.
It builds sequentially so you avoid touching ten things at once.
Confuses having a method with a guaranteed pass.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Saves the cost of deciding what to cover next.
Lets you keep moving methodically even when nervous.
Each step builds on the last, reducing rework.
Over-relying on it can blind you to actual design quality.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: this is a core benefit of the framework.
Most direct: the framework exists to handle exactly this.
Most direct: linear progress is the framework's own structure.
Not direct: a method is not a result guarantee.

scenario: 面试只有 35-45 分钟，你要在开口前决定每个环节大概花多久，才不会前面磨蹭、后面来不及深挖。
q: 补全交付框架各环节的建议用时：
text: 需求 ~{{5}} 分钟 → 核心实体 ~{{2}} 分钟 → API ~{{5}} 分钟 →（可选：数据流 ~5 分钟）→ 高层设计 ~{{10-15}} 分钟 → 深挖 ~{{10}} 分钟。
why: 这套预算把 35-45 分钟切成五段，高层设计占比最大；数字不用死记，用途是提醒你『需求和实体别磨太久，把时间留给深挖』。
why_en: The framework budgets about five minutes for requirements, two for core entities, five for the API, ten to fifteen for high-level design, and ten for deep dives, so you protect time for the deep dives.

q: 把交付框架的五个主环节按面试推进顺序排列：
steps: 高层设计（画框图，逐个 endpoint 搭建）
需求（功能性 + 非功能性）
深挖（加固设计以满足非功能需求）
API 或系统接口（定义契约）
核心实体（列出系统的关键名词）
why: 需求 → 核心实体 → API → 高层设计 → 深挖；数据处理型系统可在 API 后插入可选的『数据流』环节。
why_en: The delivery framework runs requirements, core entities, API, high-level design, and finally deep dives, with an optional data-flow step for data-processing systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求 ~5min"] --> E["核心实体 ~2min"]
    E --> A["API ~5min"]
    A -.-> D["数据流（可选）~5min"]
    A --> H["高层设计 ~10-15min"]
    D -.-> H
    H --> DD["深挖 ~10min"]

q: 功能性需求（functional requirements）的标准句式是？
options: "The system should be..."（系统应当具备…）
"Users/Clients should be able to..."（用户/客户端应能…）
"We will use..."（我们将使用…）
"The database must..."（数据库必须…）
options_en: "The system should be..."
"Users/Clients should be able to..."
"We will use..."
"The database must..."
why: 功能需求描述系统的核心特性，句式是『用户/客户端应能做 X』；它是需求环节第一个要跟考官对齐的内容。
why_en: Functional requirements are the "users should be able to" statements that capture the core features of the system.
optionMeanings: 这是非功能需求的句式，描述系统品质而非动作
这是功能需求的标准句式，描述用户能做的动作
这是技术选型陈述，不是需求陈述
这是对某个组件的约束，不是面向用户的需求
optionScenarioImpacts: 用它列需求会漏掉『用户能做什么』这条主线
直接产出可对齐优先级的功能清单
过早锁定实现细节，跳过了需求收集
把需求和某个组件强绑定，缩小了设计空间
optionDirectness: 不直接：这句式属于非功能需求。
最直接：这是功能需求教科书式的句子结构。
不直接：这是设计决策的陈述，不是需求。
不直接：这只约束了一个组件，不是完整需求。
optionMeanings_en: This phrasing describes system qualities, i.e. non-functional requirements.
This is the canonical functional-requirement phrasing describing user actions.
This states an implementation choice, not a requirement.
This constrains one component rather than stating a user-facing need.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Using this misses the core 'what can users do' thread.
Produces a feature list you can directly prioritize with the interviewer.
Locks in implementation details before requirements are even gathered.
Ties the requirement to one component, narrowing the design space.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: this phrasing belongs to non-functional requirements.
Most direct: this is the textbook functional-requirement sentence shape.
Not direct: this is a design decision, not a requirement.
Not direct: it constrains one component, not a full requirement.

q: 收集功能需求的正确姿势是？
options: 自己闷头列完再一次性宣布
被动等待面试官主动报需求
把题目原文照抄一遍当需求
像对产品经理一样提针对性问题，和考官来回对齐优先级
options_en: Silently list everything yourself and announce it all at once.
Passively wait for the interviewer to hand you the requirements.
Copy the prompt's wording verbatim as your requirements.
Ask targeted questions like a product manager and align priorities with the interviewer.
why: 需求环节常是与考官的 back-and-forth：用针对性提问逼出核心功能，并排出优先级。
why_en: Gather functional requirements by asking targeted questions as if talking to a product manager, iterating with the interviewer toward a prioritized feature list.
optionMeanings: 把需求收集当成个人任务，跳过了对齐环节
把主动权完全交给考官，自己不驱动
把已知信息复述一遍，没有产出新判断
用提问驱动，暴露隐藏假设并排优先级
optionScenarioImpacts: 考官看不到你怎么筛选和排序需求的思路
对话冷场，考官很难评估你的沟通与推理
浪费开场时间，考官得不到任何新信息
对齐后的清单成为后续设计的共同锚点
optionDirectness: 不直接：跳过了考官反馈这个关键信号源。
不直接：需求环节本该是双向互动。
不直接：复述不产生任何新判断。
最直接：提问 + 对齐正是需求环节的做法。
optionMeanings_en: Treats gathering requirements as a solo task, skipping alignment.
Hands all initiative to the interviewer instead of driving it.
Restates known information without producing new judgment.
Drives with questions that surface hidden assumptions and set priority.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer never sees how you filter and prioritize.
The conversation stalls, making it hard to assess your reasoning.
Wastes opening time without adding new information.
The aligned list becomes the shared anchor for the rest of the design.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: it skips the interviewer's feedback signal.
Not direct: the requirements step should be a two-way exchange.
Not direct: restating adds no new judgment.
Most direct: asking and aligning is exactly this step's job.

scenario: 真实产品（如 Twitter、Amazon）动辄有上百个功能，但 45 分钟的面试不可能把它们都设计一遍。
q: 面对上百个真实功能，你应该识别并聚焦前几个核心功能？
options: 10 个以上，尽量全
前 3 个左右
只挑 1 个
全部列出再筛选
options_en: Ten or more, aim for full coverage.
Roughly the top three.
Just one feature.
List every single one, then filter.
why: 你的职责是从上百个功能里挑出并优先处理 top 3 左右；这份小清单撑起接下来整场面试的设计，多了拖慢节奏、少了撑不起系统。
why_en: Your job is to identify and prioritize roughly the top three core features out of the hundreds the real product has, since that short list has to carry the rest of the interview.

q: 把功能需求列得又长又全的后果是？
options: 弊大于利——顶级大厂直接评估『聚焦重点』的能力
显得准备充分，通常会加分
对后续设计没有影响
可以直接跳过深挖环节
options_en: It backfires — top companies directly evaluate your ability to focus.
It looks thorough and usually earns bonus points.
It has no effect on the rest of the design.
It lets you skip the deep-dives step entirely.
why: 长清单会拖垮后面所有环节；不少 FAANG 把『能否聚焦最重要的事』作为直接评估项。
why_en: A long requirements list hurts more than it helps, since top companies directly evaluate your ability to focus on what matters.
optionMeanings: 长清单被当作『不会取舍』的负面信号
误以为需求越多越显得认真
误以为需求环节和后续设计彼此独立
误以为需求收集能替代后面的加固环节
optionScenarioImpacts: 每多一条需求，后面就要多验证一条，时间被稀释
考官反而会追问『这些里哪个最重要』，暴露没有取舍
实际上臃肿的需求清单会拖慢 API 和高层设计
深挖环节仍然要单独跑，需求详略换不来它
optionDirectness: 最直接：聚焦能力是大厂明确的评分项。
不直接：考官要的是取舍，不是数量。
不直接：需求清单直接决定后面设计的范围。
不直接：深挖是独立环节，不能被需求替代。
optionMeanings_en: A long list reads as a negative signal for prioritization skill.
Mistakenly assumes more requirements looks more thorough.
Mistakenly assumes the requirements step is independent of the rest.
Mistakenly assumes gathering requirements can replace hardening later.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Every extra requirement adds something to verify later, diluting time.
Interviewers will probe which one actually matters most, exposing the lack of choice.
A bloated list slows down the API and high-level design that follow.
Deep dives still have to run separately; detail here doesn't buy it back.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: focus is an explicit scoring criterion at top companies.
Not direct: interviewers want prioritization, not volume.
Not direct: the requirements list directly bounds later design scope.
Not direct: deep dives are a separate step requirements can't replace.

q: 设计 Twitter 时合理的核心功能需求有哪些？（多选）
options: 用户应能发推文
用户应能关注其他用户
用户应能看到所关注用户的推文
用户应能购买广告位
options_en: Users should be able to post tweets.
Users should be able to follow other users.
Users should be able to see tweets from users they follow.
Users should be able to purchase ad placements.
why: 发推、关注、看关注流是 Twitter 的 top 3 核心功能；广告投放不是面试 45 分钟里该抓的重点。
why_en: For Twitter the core functional requirements are posting tweets, following users, and seeing tweets from followed users.
optionMeanings: 发推是 Twitter 最基本的写路径
关注定义了用户之间的图关系
看关注流是发推之后的核心读路径
广告是变现功能，不是核心产品体验
optionScenarioImpacts: 没有发推，整个系统没有内容来源
没有关注，feed 无法定义『该展示谁的内容』
没有 feed 读取，发推和关注就没有出口
广告涉及计费、竞价，是完全独立的子系统
optionDirectness: 最直接：写路径的起点。
最直接：定义了社交图，决定谁的内容会被看到。
最直接：读路径的终点，是深挖环节的核心。
不直接：45 分钟内没有余量再设计一套广告系统。
optionMeanings_en: Posting is the most basic write path.
Following defines the graph relationship between users.
Viewing the feed is the core read path after posting.
Ads are a monetization feature, not the core product experience.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Without posting there is no content source at all.
Without following, the feed has no way to decide whose content to show.
Without feed reads, posting and following have no output.
Ads involve billing and bidding, an entirely separate subsystem.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: the starting point of the write path.
Most direct: defines the social graph that decides visibility.
Most direct: the read-path endpoint and the deep-dive centerpiece.
Not direct: there's no room in forty-five minutes for an ad system too.

q: 非功能性需求（non-functional requirements，NFR）描述的是什么？
options: 系统的功能清单
团队的开发流程
对用户重要的系统品质
运维值班安排
options_en: The list of system features.
The team's development process.
System qualities that matter to users.
The on-call rotation schedule.
why: 非功能需求刻画系统品质：可用性、扩展性、延迟等，句式是 "The system should (be able to)..."。
why_en: Non-functional requirements are statements about system qualities that matter to users, phrased as "the system should be" statements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刻画系统品质（延迟/可用性/扩展性等）而非具体动作的需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-functional requirement describes a system quality like latency or availability, not a user action.

optionMeanings: 这是功能需求的定义，不是非功能需求
这是团队管理话题，和系统品质无关
这正是非功能需求：品质而非功能
这是运维话题，不属于需求环节
optionScenarioImpacts: 混淆两者会让延迟/可用性这类品质无处安放
写进需求文档也不会被考官采纳
为后面的深挖环节提供可验证的品质目标
值班安排和设计决策无直接关系
optionDirectness: 不直接：这是『用户应能做 X』的功能需求。
不直接：不是需求收集要覆盖的内容。
最直接：品质陈述正是 NFR 的定义。
不直接：值班表与系统设计无关。
optionMeanings_en: This defines functional requirements, not non-functional ones.
A team-management topic unrelated to system qualities.
This is exactly what a non-functional requirement is: a quality, not a feature.
An operations topic, not part of requirements gathering.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Confusing the two leaves qualities like latency with nowhere to live.
Writing this down won't be accepted as a requirement by the interviewer.
Gives the deep-dives step a verifiable quality target.
On-call scheduling has no direct bearing on design decisions.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: that's a functional requirement, phrased as "users should be able to".
Not direct: not part of gathering requirements.
Most direct: a quality statement is exactly what an NFR is.
Not direct: on-call rotas are unrelated to system design.

q: 「系统应该低延迟」这条非功能需求的问题在哪？
options: 延迟根本不属于非功能需求
太空泛，需结合语境量化
这样写没问题，直接照抄即可
低延迟只和前端渲染有关
options_en: Latency isn't even a non-functional requirement.
It's too vague; it should be scoped and quantified.
It's fine as written; just copy it in as-is.
Low latency only concerns front-end rendering.
why: 好的 NFR 要放进系统语境并尽量量化：指出最需要低延迟的部分、给出目标值，否则这句话没有信息量。
why_en: Saying the system should be low latency is meaningless; a useful requirement names the part that matters and quantifies it, like search under 500 milliseconds.
optionMeanings: 把延迟错误地排除在 NFR 范畴之外
指出『空泛』才是问题所在
误把模板句当成已经写好的需求
把延迟问题限缩到某一层，缩小了范围
optionScenarioImpacts: 延迟其实是最典型的 NFR 之一，排除它会漏掉重点
量化后才能在深挖环节验证方案是否达标
空泛陈述留给后面无法验收的隐患
后端查询/网络传输同样贡献延迟，不止前端
optionDirectness: 不直接：延迟正是 NFR 里最常见的一类。
最直接：量化+语境化是这句话真正缺的东西。
不直接：几乎所有系统都『应该低延迟』，没有区分度。
不直接：延迟是端到端问题，不止前端。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly excludes latency from the NFR category.
Names vagueness as the actual problem.
Mistakes a template sentence for an already-usable requirement.
Narrows latency to one layer, shrinking the real scope.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Latency is one of the most typical NFRs, so excluding it misses the point.
Quantifying it lets the deep dives later verify whether the design meets it.
A vague statement leaves nothing checkable at the end.
Backend queries and network transfer add latency too, not just the front end.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: latency is one of the most common NFR categories.
Most direct: quantifying and scoping is exactly what's missing.
Not direct: nearly every system 'should be low latency', so it has no discriminating power.
Not direct: latency is an end-to-end concern, not only the front end.

q: 补全 Twitter 的非功能需求示例：

q: 用 CAP 定非功能需求时，正确的问法是？

Not direct: puts sensitive identity into a tamperable query parameter.
Not direct: GET shouldn't carry a write; the verb is wrong.
Not direct: swaps a trusted token for untrusted client input as the identity source.

scenario: 发推接口把当前用户写在请求体的 user_id 字段里，服务端直接读取这个字段当作作者。
q: 让客户端在请求体里传 user_id 来标识「当前用户」，隐患是什么？
options: 请求体会变大，浪费带宽
JSON 解析速度变慢
接口无法做 HTTP 缓存
任何人都能伪造别人的身份发帖
options_en: The request body gets larger, wasting bandwidth.
JSON parsing becomes slower.
The endpoint can no longer use HTTP caching.
Anyone can forge another user's identity and post as them.
why: 身份来自认证而非输入：始终从 auth token 推导当前用户，否则请求体里的 user_id 可被随意篡改冒充。
why_en: Never take the current user's identity from the request body; derive it from the authentication token, or anyone can impersonate anyone.
codeSample:
# 不安全：身份来自可篡改的请求体
POST /v1/tweets
body: { "user_id": "123", "text": "hi" }

# 安全：身份来自认证 token
POST /v1/tweets
Authorization: Bearer <token>
body: { "text": "hi" }   # user 从 token 解出

termDefinitions.meaning: 认证后颁发的凭证，服务端应从它推导当前用户，而不是信任请求体字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An auth token is issued after authentication, and the server should derive the current user from it rather than trusting a body field.

optionMeanings: 把安全隐患误判成性能上的带宽开销
把安全隐患误判成解析性能问题
把安全隐患误判成缓存能力的丧失
指出一个字段可以被随意篡改带来的身份伪造风险
optionScenarioImpacts: 多一个 user_id 字段带来的带宽开销可以忽略不计
多解析一个短字符串字段不构成性能瓶颈
POST 创建类接口本来就很少被 HTTP 缓存
攻击者只需改一个字段就能以他人身份发帖
optionDirectness: 不直接：带宽增量微不足道，不是真正的风险点。
不直接：解析开销可忽略，不是安全问题。
不直接：这类接口原本就不依赖 HTTP 缓存。
最直接：这正是『信任客户端身份声明』的核心风险。
optionMeanings_en: Misreads the security risk as a bandwidth cost.
Misreads the security risk as a parsing-performance issue.
Misreads the security risk as lost caching ability.
Names the impersonation risk of trusting a field anyone can edit.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The bandwidth added by one extra user_id field is negligible.
Parsing one more short string field is not a performance bottleneck.
POST create endpoints rarely rely on HTTP caching anyway.
An attacker only has to edit one field to post as someone else.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: the bandwidth increase is negligible, not the real risk.
Not direct: parsing overhead is negligible, not a security issue.
Not direct: this kind of endpoint never relied on HTTP caching.
Most direct: this is exactly the risk of trusting a client-declared identity.

q: REST 资源命名的惯例是？
options: 复数名词（/tweets 而不是 /tweet）
动词短语（/createTweet）
全大写路径（/TWEETS）
命名随意，怎么写都行
options_en: Plural nouns, like /tweets instead of /tweet.
Verb phrases, like /createTweet.
All-uppercase paths, like /TWEETS.
Naming doesn't matter — anything goes.
why: REST 把系统建模成资源集合：路径用复数名词表示事物集合，动作交给 HTTP 动词表达。
why_en: REST resources are plural nouns representing things in your system, with actions expressed by HTTP verbs.
codeSample:
GET  /v1/tweets        # list
GET  /v1/tweets/{id}   # read one
POST /v1/tweets        # create (verb is the HTTP method, not the path)
optionMeanings: 路径命名事物集合，动作交给 HTTP 方法
把动作硬编码进路径，和 REST 的资源模型冲突
只是排版风格，不影响是否符合 REST 惯例
放弃任何一致性，接口会因人而异难以维护
optionScenarioImpacts: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE 同一个 /tweets 路径就能表达全部操作
动词一多，路径集合会膨胀成一堆不一致的端点
大小写不是 REST 惯例关心的维度
团队协作时每个人风格不同，接口难以预测
optionDirectness: 最直接：这是 REST 资源命名的标准惯例。
不直接：违反了『动词交给 HTTP 方法』的原则。
不直接：大小写与是否符合 REST 无关。
不直接：一致性正是 REST 惯例存在的意义。
optionMeanings_en: Paths name a collection of things; actions belong to the HTTP method.
Hardcodes an action into the path, conflicting with REST's resource model.
Just a formatting style, unrelated to REST compliance.
Abandons consistency, making endpoints unpredictable across a team.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE on the same /tweets path expresses every operation.
More verbs means a sprawling set of inconsistent endpoints.
Casing isn't a dimension REST convention cares about.
Different styles per teammate make the API hard to predict.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct: this is the standard REST naming convention.
Not direct: violates the principle that verbs belong to the HTTP method.
Not direct: casing has nothing to do with REST compliance.
Not direct: consistency is the entire point of having a convention.

scenario: 你在设计网页爬虫：系统本质是对输入执行一长串处理步骤、产出结果的数据处理系统。
q: API 之后、高层设计之前，可选做的一步是？
options: 直接开始容量估算
用简单列表描述数据流
先写单元测试
先画完整 ER 图
options_en: Jump straight into capacity estimation.
List the data flow as a simple sequence of actions.
Write unit tests first.
Draw the complete ER diagram first.
why: 数据处理型系统值得先列数据流（约 5 分钟），它会直接支撑接下来的高层设计。
why_en: For data-processing systems, optionally spend five minutes listing the high-level sequence of actions the system performs.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统没有长动作序列（普通 CRUD 产品），直接跳过数据流环节，进入高层设计。
tradeoff: 先列数据流『多花 5 分钟，换高层设计更顺』 vs 跳过它『省时间，仅适合无长处理链的系统』

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述实体及其相互关系的图示，通常在数据模型定案后画。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ER diagram shows entities and their relationships, usually drawn once the data model is settled.

optionMeanings: 把估算当成这一步该做的事，和数据流无关
把处理管线拆成一份高层动作清单
把测试环节提前到设计尚未成形的阶段
把细节建模提前到还没画高层设计的阶段
optionScenarioImpacts: 估算在这里没有触发条件，属于误用环节
这份清单会直接变成高层设计里的组件序列
接口和架构都还没定，测试无从针对性编写
字段关系随后仍会因高层设计而调整，过早画图会被推翻
optionDirectness: 不直接：这里没有需要当场算的数字。
最直接：数据流清单正是为数据处理系统准备的可选步骤。
不直接：测试属于实现阶段，不是设计交付环节。
不直接：ER 图排在核心实体和高层设计之后。
optionMeanings_en: Treats estimation as this step's task, unrelated to data flow.
Breaks the processing pipeline into a high-level list of actions.
Pulls testing forward before the design has even taken shape.
Pulls detailed modeling forward before high-level design is drawn.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Estimation has no trigger here; it's a misuse of this step.
This list becomes the component sequence in the high-level design.
Neither the API nor architecture exist yet, so tests have nothing to target.
Field relationships will still shift with high-level design, so this gets redrawn.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct: there's no number here that needs calculating on the spot.
Most direct: a data-flow list is exactly the optional step for data-processing systems.
Not direct: testing belongs to implementation, not the design delivery.
Not direct: an ER diagram comes after core entities and high-level design.

q: 把网页爬虫的数据流排成正确顺序：
why: 爬虫数据流：取种子 URL → 解析 HTML → 提取 URL → 存数据 → 重复。这份清单直接指导高层设计。
why_en: A web crawler fetches seed URLs, parses the HTML, extracts new URLs, stores the data, and repeats.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Seed["Seed URL"] --> Fetch["Fetch HTML"]

    Store --> Seed

q: 高层设计（~10-15 分钟）环节的核心产出是？
options: 可运行的代码
完整的成本预算
框和箭头：组件及其交互
详细的部署脚本

A complete cost budget.

optionMeanings: 把这一步误当成实现阶段
把这一步误当成财务规划
点出组件图这个正确产出

Mistakes this step for writing operations scripts.

Cost budgeting almost never appears as a scoring point in these interviews.
The component diagram directly answers how each API request gets satisfied.
Deployment scripts go down to implementation detail, beyond this ten-to-fifteen-minute step.

Not direct: cost budgeting isn't this step's goal.

Not direct: deployment scripts are implementation detail, not this step.

scenario: 进入高层设计，面对空白画布不知从何画起，担心漏掉需求。
q: 最稳的推进方式是？
options: 先把所有可能用到的组件都摆上画布
从数据库开始，向外逐步补充
先画好全球多机房容灾方案
逐个过 API endpoint 搭建组件
options_en: Put every component you might possibly need on the canvas first.
Start from the database and build outward.
Draw a global multi-region disaster-recovery setup first.
Go through API endpoints one by one, building components.
why: 多数情况下可以逐 endpoint 顺序搭建：每个接口需要什么组件就补什么，天然保证设计对齐需求。
why_en: Go through your API endpoints one by one and build up the design sequentially to satisfy each of them.
whenOtherWins: 数据处理型系统（如爬虫）按 data flow 的步骤顺序推进更自然，而不是按 endpoint。
tradeoff: 逐 endpoint 搭建『天然贴合需求，但节奏依赖 API 清晰度』 vs 一次性堆全部组件『看似全面，实际容易偏离需求』
optionMeanings: 把『覆盖全面』误当成推进方式
把数据库当成设计的起点而非终点
把深挖阶段的加固内容提前搬进高层设计
把 API 清单当作驱动设计的顺序表
optionScenarioImpacts: 很多组件到最后用不上，等于提前浪费时间画蛇添足
容易先陷入表结构细节，反而忘了先满足接口需求
多机房容灾属于非功能需求的深挖内容，过早引入会拖慢节奏
每加一个组件都能直接对应一条需求，不容易偏题
optionDirectness: 不直接：容易堆砌出用不上的组件。
不直接：容易本末倒置，先纠结存储细节。
不直接：容灾属于深挖，不是高层设计的起点。

Starts from the database as the beginning rather than the end.
Pulls deep-dive hardening content forward into high-level design.
Uses the API list as the ordered driver of the design.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Many components end up unused, wasting time drawing things you don't need.
You get stuck in table-structure detail and forget to satisfy the endpoints first.
Multi-region resilience is deep-dive, non-functional content; pulling it forward stalls momentum.
Each added component maps directly to a requirement, keeping the design on track.

Not direct: tends to get lost in storage detail before the requirements are met.

q: 高层设计阶段过早堆复杂度（缓存、队列全上）最常见的下场是？

深挖环节本就需要单独时间逐条对照 NFR，省不掉
考官通常只提问和观察，不会替你简化设计
optionDirectness: 最直接：这正是『过早复杂化』的典型代价。
不直接：堆砌不等于完善，反而可能做不完。

不直接：简化设计是候选人自己的职责。

Wrongly assumes the interviewer will simplify the design for you.

Interviewers care more about meeting core functionality than component count.

Interviewers mostly observe and probe; they won't simplify the design for you.

Not direct: deep-dive time is reserved separately, not saved by doing it early.
Not direct: simplifying the design is the candidate's own responsibility.

q: 画高层设计时，嘴上应该同步讲什么？

Puts the narration focus on irrelevant release-year trivia.
